The condition for S to contain a product was clearly artificial and in the historical note in [5], Chapter IV, Lang remarks: “In extending Theorems 1, 2, 3, one has the following possibilities. First, a suggestion of Nagata, that the set S in Theorem 1 may be described as contained in a hypersurface (algebraic). This would be a good way of eliminating the unnatural condition that S be a product. (One would also need to bound the degree of the hypersurface.)” This is exactly what we do in our Theorem A.
